title: The Man Who Built K-Pop Just Declared War on His Own Company — Lee Soo-man's A2O Enter Korea Is Coming for SM and HYBE
excerpt: Three years of enforced silence are over. SM Entertainment founder Lee Soo-man has launched A2O Enter Korea in Cheongdam-dong, Gangnam — just steps from SM's headquarters — and announced a new boy group debut in the first half of 2026. Yoo Young-jin has joined him. The K-pop power map is being redrawn.
author: MEARROW Editorial Desk
content:
In February 2023, Lee Soo-man was pushed out of the company he had spent 30 years building. He sold his 14.8% stake in SM Entertainment to HYBE for 422.8 billion KRW, and as part of the deal, he signed a three-year non-compete clause — barring him from domestic music production in Korea.

That three years ended in late February 2026.

And he moved immediately.

## A2O Enter Korea — Entering Gangnam

### A New Label in the Heart of Seoul

Lee Soo-man has officially established **A2O Enter Korea** in Cheongdam-dong, Gangnam, Seoul — the Korean arm of his Singapore-headquartered A2O Entertainment. Having already built outposts in the US, China, and Japan, A2O is now entering the Korean market directly.

The location is symbolic. Cheongdam-dong is also home to SM Entertainment's headquarters. Lee Soo-man set up his new company in front of the building that used to be his.

### Yoo Young-jin Has Joined

The most striking development is the personnel move: **Yoo Young-jin** has joined A2O Enter Korea.

Yoo Young-jin is the man who practically defined SM's sonic identity. TVXQ's ballads, Girls' Generation's "Genie," EXO's "MAMA," SHINee's signature tracks — the concept of "SM Sound" only exists because of Yoo Young-jin's composing and arranging. His departure from SM and reunion with Lee Soo-man is not just a hiring decision. **It's the original K-pop engine being rebooted.**

Girls' Generation's **Sunny (Lee Soon-kyu)**, Lee Soo-man's niece, is also involved in the venture.

## A Boy Group Is Coming in the First Half of 2026

### His First Male Group Since NCT

The last boy group Lee Soo-man personally launched was **NCT** in 2016. Now, a decade later, a new boy group will debut under his creative direction.

A2O Enter Korea has confirmed a boy group debut in the first half of 2026. Unlike A2O's previous international-focused projects, this group is designed to **compete directly in the Korean domestic market** — the same battlefield as SM, HYBE, JYP, and YG.

### The Industry Is Already Watching

Media reaction was immediate. From the Korea Herald to allkpop to Koreaboo, major outlets declared that "the K-pop power map is being redrawn." One industry insider put it bluntly: *"This isn't just one producer returning. This is the person who invented the K-pop system announcing he's going to fight it."*

## Lee Soo-man vs SM vs HYBE vs Min Hee-jin — The Battle Lines Are Drawn

### The 2023 Collapse

What happened in early 2023 was unprecedented in K-pop history. SM Entertainment's board moved to strip Lee of his influence by introducing a multi-production center system. Lee retaliated by selling his stake to HYBE, briefly making them SM's largest shareholder. But Kakao countered with a public tender offer and ultimately secured management control. HYBE quietly stepped back, participating in Kakao's offer and walking away with a profit. Lee Soo-man was left standing alone.

HYBE included the non-compete clause in their purchase agreement. Three years of domestic silence. That's now over.

### The Current Battleground

The K-pop landscape Lee Soo-man is returning to in 2026 is more complex than it was in 2023.

- **SM Entertainment** (majority owner: Kakao): The company he founded. Currently in the middle of launching SMTR25, a new boy group project being introduced through the Mnet reality show "Reply High School." A direct competitive collision with A2O's boy group is now inevitable.
- **HYBE**: The company that wrote the non-compete clause into his exit agreement. Now facing Lee's return while still dealing with the internal fallout from the NewJeans/ADOR dispute.
- **Min Hee-jin**: Operating independently after her conflict with HYBE, Min Hee-jin's trajectory is also part of the competitive reshuffle that Lee's return accelerates.

In one return, Lee Soo-man has opened a three-front war.

## MEARROW's Take on Lee Soo-man's Return

The system Lee Soo-man built is not complicated to describe: rigorous trainee development → structured debut → fandom infrastructure → global scaling. That framework is essentially what HYBE, JYP, and their competitors run today. Lee Soo-man built the original. Everyone else followed.

He's walking back in with the same playbook. The difference this time is that **he's competing against the companies that inherited it from him**.

Two success variables matter most. First: whether Yoo Young-jin's involvement translates into genuine musical quality that resonates in 2026. His productions defined second-generation K-pop's sonic language — but how today's listeners respond to that sensibility is an open question. Second: whether the new group can build an independent fanbase beyond the name recognition of its creator.

Getting industry attention has already happened. The harder part comes next.

Lee Soo-man's return is now the most closely watched project in the K-pop industry. When A2O Enter Korea's first boy group takes the stage, the power map will be redrawn — again.
